title: 10 CalmBoxes for Rite Path
purpose: To put a CalmBox within reach of every youth and staff member in the residential program Rite Path supports, on both the girls' and boys' sides.
summary: Rite Path Behavioral Health has served about 1,000 people a year across the Phoenix area since 2020, and this project puts 10 CalmBoxes in the residential program it supports. A CalmBox is a small, personal device, FDA-cleared for anxiety and insomnia. Rite Path's staff already use the 2 they have several times a day, and 10 more means up to 45 youth and their staff can reach one whenever they need it.
whatWeFund: 10 CalmBoxes ($300 each) for the residential program Rite Path supports: 5 for the girls' side and 5 for the boys' side, shared by up to 45 youth and the 6–10 staff who care for them. Once funded, this project closes and additional gifts go to the next open project.
whyThisPopulation:
Many of the youth in this program arrive having lived through abuse, neglect, loss, or a home that was never steady. Day to day, they're living apart from their families, unsure what comes next, and learning to trust adults again. Their bodies learned to stay on guard long before anyone asked them to heal.

That's the part therapy alone can't reach. Rite Path's clinicians teach coping skills and build safe relationships, but the work needs a regulated nervous system underneath it. A youth whose body won't stand down can't take in the rest.

Rite Path already knows what a CalmBox does. Their staff have used 2 for two years, several times a day, with clients and in staff trainings. Clinical Program Manager Britnee Snow says the first thing she notices is body language: watching "the body loosen its grip and melt into relaxation." Two boxes can't stretch across 45 youth on two sides of a residential program. Ten can.
